name: Secluded Beach
notes: Clear, high-contrast morning-afternoon coastal light. Recommend NOT shipping to the browser; use as a Blender lighting reference only, or bake an offline heavily-downsampled equirect (untested).

name: Casuarina (no CC0 model found)
notes: Casuarina equisetifolia is the actual dominant coastal species at Mahabalipuram, and no CC0 3D model exists for it on Poly Haven, ambientCG (no models category at all), Quaternius, Kenney, or Sketchfab's CC0-tagged results (checked; only generic pine/tree packs and a paid RenderHub listing surfaced). This is a confirmed absence, not an unsearched gap. Aligns with the project's own stated pattern of declaring what is invented rather than faking a match.

Not recommended for any use here.

name: @gltf-transform/cli
license: MIT (tool itself; does not affect licensing of processed assets)
notes: npm registry confirms latest 4.5.0, published 2026-09-01. Pure npm/npx, no separate native binary needed for draco/meshopt/resize/webp (webp needs `sharp`, pulled in automatically). KTX2 (etc1s/uastc) commands additionally require installing KTX-Software's `toktx` binary separately -- not pure npm. Commands verified by reading the actual CLI source (packages/cli/src/cli.ts) on GitHub, not just docs prose: `gltf-transform draco <in> <out> [--method edgebreaker|sequential] [--quantize-position 1-16, default 14] [...]`; `gltf-transform meshopt <in> <out> [--level medium|high, default high] [...]`; `gltf-transform resize <in> <out> --width <px> --height <px>`; `gltf-transform webp <in> <out>`; `gltf-transform etc1s|uastc <in> <out>` (requires toktx).

name: Meshopt geometry compression, tested against the project's real GLB
notes: RECOMMENDED: highest-leverage, lowest-risk delivery optimization available for this project today. Ran directly against assets/models/mamallapuram-monuments.glb via npx (no repo changes made). 44% gzip reduction (301,860 -> 167,796 B) for a 6,460 B gzipped decoder -- net ~128 KB win on first load, cacheable across pages. All 722 mesh primitives and 53 materials preserved unchanged.

name: Draco geometry compression, tested against the project's real GLB
notes: NOT recommended over meshopt for this project. Real gzip cut is 85,269 B (301,860 -> 216,591), but the required decoder (draco_decoder.wasm + draco_wasm_wrapper.js) costs 74,774-99,892 B gzipped depending on which pairing is used -- meshopt's decoder is 11-15x smaller for a larger net win on this specific file. Draco tends to win more decisively on single dense meshes (e.g. photogrammetry scans); this project's 722 small architectural primitives are closer to meshopt's sweet spot.

name: gltf-transform optimize (aggressive default pipeline) -- tested, flagged as unsafe here

filesize.mesh_primitives_result: 722 -> 1 (all meshes joined into one, verified via gltf-transform inspect)

notes: Tested for completeness. Produces a dramatic 10x reduction (30,813 B gzip) but only because its default pipeline runs `join` (merges all meshes into one, destroying per-mesh identity) and `simplify` (reduces vertex count). This project's buildMassing code suppresses extruded footprints by matching modelled monuments by name/mesh, and re-anchors map markers to the measured top of specific meshes after load -- both would very likely break if all 722 primitives became 1. Do not use `optimize` blind; use the plain `meshopt` command in isolation, or explicitly disable `--join`/`--simplify` and re-test the site-marker and exclude-logic code before adopting.

name: MeshoptDecoder (three.js examples/jsm/libs)
notes: Downloaded from cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.169.0 (the project's vendored version) and measured directly. Tiny -- the single biggest practical argument for meshopt over Draco on this project.

name: DRACOLoader decoder files (three.js examples/jsm/libs/draco)

name: Basis/KTX2 transcoder (three.js examples/jsm/libs/basis)
notes: Downloaded from cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.169.0 and measured directly. Total ~260 KB gzipped -- a large fixed cost, more than this project's entire current gzipped 3D model, that only pays off once several textured assets are shipped (not for one small texture).

name: three.js version audit
notes: Vendored in project (assets/vendor/three.module.js): r169, published 2024-09-26 (per npm registry time data for three@0.169.0). Current latest: r185.1, published 2026-07-01 (npm dist-tags.latest). 16 minor revisions / ~22 months behind. Checked official Migration Guide r169->r185 for breaking changes relevant to this project's actual API usage (GLTFLoader, OrbitControls, WebGLRenderer, lights -- no WebGPU/TSL found in scene-3d.js): OrbitControls.connect() became mandatory with a DOM element (r173->r174); OrbitControls keyboard input now requires explicit listenToKeyEvents() (r177->r178); RGBELoader renamed to HDRLoader (r179->r180, relevant only if HDRI work ships); Object3D.dispose() added (r184->r185, unused today). Not a risk-free drop-in upgrade -- OrbitControls call sites need checking at minimum.

name: <model-viewer> web component
notes: Current version 4.3.1 (npm registry, published 2026-06-04). Downloaded and measured the actual CDN dist/model-viewer.min.js. At 288 KB gzip, it is bigger on its own than this project's entire current vendored three.js+GLTFLoader stack (365,552 + 110,040 B raw, uncompressed comparison but the size direction holds). Not a fit as a replacement for scene-3d.js's custom scroll-driven camera/terrain/globe/diorama scene, which needs raw three.js access that model-viewer deliberately abstracts away. Would only make sense as a complement -- e.g. a separate standalone single-monument AR-viewer page -- not as a swap-in.

name: gltfpack (meshoptimizer CLI)
notes: npm registry confirms latest 1.2.0, published 2026-06-30. Basic usage: `gltfpack -i scene.gltf -o scene.glb`; `-cc` enables meshopt compression, `-tc` converts textures to KTX2, `-si R` simplifies mesh to ratio R. Not run directly against the project's file in this research pass -- @gltf-transform/cli's `meshopt` command was used instead and gave the measured numbers above. gltfpack additionally does mesh merging/simplification more aggressively by default, similar caution as gltf-transform's `optimize` command applies.
